answer.summary: For a one-sided pooled two-sample t-test comparing two independent normal means with equal variances: expected difference 4.3 dBA, common SD 7.8 dBA, 32 participants per group (64 total), α = 0.05, the statistical power is **0.7040583526690912** (approximately **70.41%**). There is approximately a 70.41% probability of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis if the true mean difference equals 4.3 dBA under the assumed parameters.
answer.method: Analytical power calculation via R's stats::power.t.test() for a two-sample pooled Student's t-test, verified by non-centrality parameter method. Test specification: one-sided alternative H₁: μ₁ > μ₂, significance level α = 0.05. The non-centrality parameter λ = (expected_difference) / (common_sd × √(2/n)) = 4.3 / (7.8 × √(2/32)) = 2.2051. Under H₁, the test statistic follows a non-central t-distribution with df = 62 and noncentrality λ = 2.2051. Power = P(t₆₂ > t₀.₀₅,₆₂ | λ = 2.2051) = P(t₆₂ > 1.6698 | λ = 2.2051) = 0.704058.

limitations: Power estimate assumes exact normality; robustness to non-normal distributions (especially heavy tails or extreme skewness) not evaluated
Assumes equal variances; if true variances differ appreciably, Welch's t-test (unequal variance) may be preferable and would yield slightly higher power
No adjustment for multiple testing if this is part of a larger study

# Compute power for one-sided pooled t-test
# H0: mu_treatment = mu_control vs. H1: mu_treatment > mu_control
# Two independent normal groups with equal variances

# Parameters
expected_difference <- 4.3  # dBA
common_sd <- 7.8            # dBA
n_per_group <- 32           # participants
alpha <- 0.05               # significance level
sided <- "one.sided"        # direction: one-sided test

# Use stats::power.t.test for two-sample t-test with equal variances
# effect = delta / sigma (Cohen's d)
effect_size <- expected_difference / common_sd

power_result <- power.t.test(
  n = n_per_group,
  delta = expected_difference,
  sd = common_sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = sided
)

# Extract power
power <- power_result$power

# Calculate degrees of freedom for reference
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2

# Calculate standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- expected_difference / common_sd

cat("Power Analysis: Two-Sample Pooled t-Test (One-Sided)\n")
cat("="*60, "\n")

cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d\n", 2*n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Test type: Two-sample pooled t-test (one-sided)\n"))
cat("="*60, "\n")
cat("Derived Quantities:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Cohen's d (effect size): %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("  Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat("="*60, "\n")
cat("Result:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", power))
cat("="*60, "\n")

# Output for submission
results_df <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"

# Verification using non-centrality parameter approach
# For two-sample t-test with equal variances

expected_difference <- 4.3  # dBA
common_sd <- 7.8            # dBA
n_per_group <- 32           # participants
alpha <- 0.05               # significance level

# Non-centrality parameter (λ)
# For two-sample t-test: λ = δ / (σ√(2/n)) where δ is expected difference
lambda <- expected_difference / (common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group))

# Degrees of freedom
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
# For one-sided test (right-tailed): t_crit = t_{α,df}
t_crit <- qt(p = 1 - alpha, df = df, lower.tail = TRUE)

# Power is P(t > t_crit | H1 true) = P(t_nc(λ, df) > t_crit)
# where t_nc is non-central t distribution
power_nc <- 1 - pt(q = t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)

cat("Verification: Non-Centrality Parameter Method\n")
cat("=====================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", lambda))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical value (t_{1-α,df}): %.4f\n", t_crit))
cat(sprintf("Power (1 - P(t ≤ t_crit | λ)): %.6f\n", power_nc))
cat("=====================================================\n")

# Compare with power.t.test result
cat("Comparison with power.t.test:\n")
cat(sprintf("  power.t.test result: 0.704058\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality result: %.6f\n", power_nc))
cat(sprintf("  Difference: %.10f\n", abs(power_nc - 0.704058)))
